instruction: Extract the audio from a video file and save it as 'audio.mp3' in the same folder.

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting audio from video file using VLC. The evaluator checks if audio.mp3 file was created with valid content (size > 10KB and duration > 1 second). Similar complexity to original subtitle extraction task.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts audio file state (existence, size, duration) from the specified path
Getter uses appropriate tools (ffprobe for duration, stat for size) to extract audio metadata
Metric logic can verify the core requirement: audio file was successfully extracted
WARNING: Metric function ignores the 'expected' parameter entirely. When expected.type='rule', the framework passes the rules dict directly, but the metric never uses it
WARNING: Metric uses hardcoded thresholds (10KB size, 1 second duration) instead of reading from 'expected' parameter
The expected.rules.file_should_exist is defined but never checked by the metric function
Despite ignoring 'expected', the hardcoded logic can still semantically verify the task (file exists, has content, has audio duration)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Metric should check expected.get('file_should_exist') to determine if file existence is required
Consider adding configurable thresholds in expected.rules (e.g., 'min_size_bytes', 'min_duration_seconds') instead of hardcoding 10KB and 1 second
Update metric to use expected parameter: 'if expected.get('file_should_exist', True) and not result.get('exists'): return 0.0'
